title: Selection is a system
summary: This lesson covers building robust data table selection systems, focusing on tri-state checkboxes, explicit selection counts, and state persistence. It also advocates for using undo functionality over confirmation modals for destructive bulk actions.

transcript.text: Tick the header box, all 247 rows come with it. Selection is a system.
Your header checkbox has three states, not two. Checked, empty, and partial. Drop the partial state and users lose track of what they picked.
Clicking that partial box selects everything, never clears it.
Select all grabs the six rows on screen. There are 247 in the table. Say the number out loud. Select all 247 matching.
A filter moves that number so the label reads it live.
Shift click picks a range, and every desktop user expects it. Then they change page and the selection dies.
Selection lives in your app state, not in the visible rows.
Deleting 247 rows needs no confirm modal. Echo the count inside the button, run it, then offer undo for 10 seconds. Reversible beats careful.
Follow for more UX systems. Save this for your next data table.

on_screen_text: TRI-STATE: The header box has three states.
partial is a state, not a bug
SELECT ALL: Six on screen. 247 in the table.
RANGE + PERSIST: Shift picks a range. Paging keeps it.
BULK DESTRUCTIVE: Echo the count. Offer undo.
Three states: Empty, partial, checked — the dash is not optional
Name the number: "Select all 247 matching", never a bare "all"
Selection is state: Shift ranges and paging keep the ids alive
Undo, not confirm: Echo the count, run it, offer ten seconds back
design_principles: Tri-state checkboxes (empty, partial, checked) are essential for header selection.
Explicitly name the total count in 'Select All' actions to avoid ambiguity.
Selection state must persist across pagination.
Reversible actions (Undo) are superior to friction-heavy confirmation modals.
before_after: A standard table selection vs. a comprehensive selection system with tri-states, persisted state, and undo functionality.
